translations.answer: Confirm the target is the nv×nv matrix obtained from the space wrench λ contraction, not the full dJ/dq. The original thread indicates that the external-force term in RNEA includes J^Tλ, so the derivative d(J^Tλ)/dq can be directly calculated using RNEA analytical derivatives. The original author of Valkyrie nv=32 confirmed this method and reported that the derivative call is approximately 0.035 ms; these times are only representative of the old environment and should not be extrapolated.
translations.applicability: Applies to the specific contraction of d(J^Tλ)/dq in contact QP; original post is for Valkyrie nv=32 and 2019 API. The current signature must be verified against the target Pinocchio version.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author first used RBDL finite difference and discussed the full tensor API and nv time-variation calls.
translations.details.attempts.1: Subsequently, the RNEA derivatives for zero gravity, zero velocity/acceleration, and external force terms were used for dJ^T/dq·λ.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, write the real expression as J(q+dq)^T λ and confirm that the target is d(J^T λ)/dq, not the full dJ/dq.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguish between the Hessian-vector product of the tensor's last dimension and the nv×nv result from the original post along the space wrench dimension.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: If the target is indeed d(J^T λ)/dq, use the RNEA analytical derivatives with external forces directly, rather than first constructing the full frame Hessian.
translations.details.environments.0: 2019 Pinocchio/RBDL comparison; Valkyrie humanoid, nv=32; author only mentioned standard laptop, no CPU or precise Pinocchio version provided.
translations.details.limits.0: 0.500/0.060/0.035 ms is a single author, old version, and unspecified CPU thread record; cannot be used as a current hardware benchmark.
translations.details.limits.1: Maintainer estimates a standard laptop could reach 0.015 ms, but the author did not verify this value, and it is not included as a result here.
translations.details.limits.2: If optimization truly requires the full dJ/dq, use the Pinocchio 4 frame kinematic Hessian interface instead of this contraction.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author explicitly confirmed that RNEA derivatives can obtain the required Hessian-wrench product and reported the native Valkyrie comparison time sequence.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How to avoid explicitly constructing the 6×nv×nv full kinematic Hessian during linearization of the contact QP using J(q+dq)^T λ?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Compare the analytical contraction with finite difference in random q and λ directions before incorporating it into real-time contact QP.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Explicit construction of the full Hessian would calculate unnecessary elements for the optimizer; RNEA external force term already includes J^T λ, so its analytical derivative can directly provide the required contraction.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The full Hessian from finite difference impedes about 1 ms of computational budget; the actual target is to contract the first dimension of the Hessian and the contact wrench λ to obtain an nv×nv matrix.
translations.source.locator: Pinocchio #867: Comment 526278645 explains the contraction and RNEA relationship; Comment 530373296 confirms its applicability and provides a comparison; Comment 530407733 adds the raw call sequence.
translations.source.title: Pinocchio RNEA derivatives can avoid constructing the full Hessian during linearization of J(q+dq)^T λ in contact QP.
